Instead, Subtract the part you do not want (for example a brick on each side to cut away), or draw the common shape as an extruded polygon or a polyhedron.

checks.explain.air-pad: The open boundaries absorb the outgoing wave only if they stand far enough from the structure; with the air padding this small the reflections from them, and the box the far field is computed on, come too near the antenna. Use about a quarter wavelength at f min, which the automatic padding gives when the field is left empty.
checks.explain.boolean-cut-erases: A cut-out (a subtracted curved shape) is a vacuum shape above its host solid, so everything with the same or a lower priority inside it is erased too, not only the host. Raise the priority of a solid that must stay inside the cut-out, such as a pin or the substrate.
checks.explain.boolean-cut-reach: A cut-out only removes what it reaches. This one leaves a gap to a zero-thickness sheet of its own solid, or has no thickness itself, so the sheet stays whole there. Let the cut-out touch or cross the sheet, and give it a thickness.
checks.explain.brick-flat: The brick has no area because two or more dimensions are zero. Give it extent along at least two axes; one zero dimension is allowed for a sheet.
checks.explain.brick-inverted: A minimum coordinate is above its maximum, so the shape bounds are reversed. Swap the coordinates or correct the expressions that set them.
checks.explain.build: The server could not build the simulation geometry or settings, so no valid preview can be produced. Correct the field or unsupported geometry described in the message and try the preview again.
checks.explain.cells-per-wavelength: Too few cells cannot accurately represent the changing electromagnetic fields. Set a positive resolution, usually at least 15 cells per wavelength, and check convergence with a finer mesh.
checks.explain.component-path: An empty folder name makes the component hierarchy ambiguous. Use nonempty names separated by slashes, such as antenna/feed, or leave the whole path empty.
checks.explain.conductivity: A metal's conductivity must be positive to describe a lossy conductor. Enter it in S/m (copper 5.8e7, aluminium 3.5e7, gold 4.1e7), or leave it empty for a perfect conductor.
checks.explain.cone-length: The cone needs a positive axial length to define a volume. Put its range minimum below its maximum.
checks.explain.cone-radii: With both radii zero the cone collapses to a line and has no volume. Give at least one end a positive radius.
checks.explain.copies: The copy count is invalid or produces more geometry than the designer allows. Use a whole number of zero or more and reduce combined transforms to at most 1000 copies.
checks.explain.cut-all: The cuts remove the entire sheet, leaving no conductor or material there. Reduce or move the cuts if any of the sheet should remain.
checks.explain.cut-sheet: A rectangle cut must lie in the plane of the sheet it removes material from. Make start and stop equal on exactly one axis and give the other two axes a positive extent.
checks.explain.cut-unsupported: A cut removes area from flat sheets in its plane (rectangular sheets, polygons, flat circles), not volume from a solid. The cut plane crosses a solid of this part: make that shape a sheet, or carve it with a Boolean subtract.
checks.explain.cut-unused: This cut touches no flat sheet in its plane, so it removes nothing. Move it onto the intended sheet and check that its outline overlaps the sheet.
checks.explain.cylinder-length: The cylinder axis has no valid length, so it cannot define a volume. Separate its endpoints or put the range minimum below the maximum.
checks.explain.end-criterion: The stop threshold measures how far the field energy has decayed below its peak, in dB. Fairbeam accepts -10 to -300 dB, because a run stopped above -10 dB has not meaningfully decayed. Use about -40 dB for a quick look and -60 dB for accurate S-parameters and efficiency.
checks.explain.eps-r: Relative permittivity below one is outside the dielectric model supported here. Use a value of at least one from the material data at your operating frequency.
checks.explain.excitation-too-long: The excitation pulse uses too much of the timestep budget, leaving too little time for fields to decay and results to converge. Model thin metal as sheets, coarsen the finest detail, or increase max timesteps and check convergence.
checks.explain.expr: This value cannot be evaluated, so the geometry or simulation setting is unknown. Enter a valid number or expression and check its parameter names.
checks.explain.f-min: The simulated band must start above zero for the excitation and frequency results to be meaningful. Set a positive minimum frequency in GHz.
checks.explain.f-order: An empty or reversed frequency band cannot define the simulation. Set the maximum frequency above the minimum.
checks.explain.f-ratio: A very wide band combines a fine mesh with a long simulation time. Narrow the band to the frequencies you need or split it into separate runs.
checks.explain.ff-band: A far-field result outside the simulated band is not reliable. Move this frequency into the band or expand the simulation band to include it.
checks.explain.field-plane: A field plane records E or H at a few frequencies inside the simulated band, and each map adds to the run's memory and result size. Give each plane one to four frequencies within the band and use at most four planes.
checks.explain.field-plane-position: A field plane outside the simulation domain cannot be recorded where it was placed; the run would record it at the domain's edge instead. Move the plane's position inside the domain shown by the 3D view's domain box.
checks.explain.inner-radius: The tube needs a wall between its inner and outer radii. Set the inner radius to zero for a solid cylinder or to a positive value smaller than the outer radius.
checks.explain.linpoly-length: A zero extrusion length leaves a flat polygon instead of a solid. Enter a nonzero length if you intended a volume, or keep it flat intentionally.
checks.explain.mesh-cells: A large mesh needs more memory and time and may exceed the server's cell limit. Reduce cells per wavelength, lower the maximum frequency, or simplify fine details while checking accuracy.
checks.explain.mesh-feature: This feature falls between mesh lines and may disappear from the simulated geometry. Thicken it, model thin metal as a sheet, or refine the mesh until it is resolved.
checks.explain.mesh-lines: Manual mesh lines need at least two finite, strictly increasing coordinates on each axis. Correct the line list or switch to automatic mesh.
checks.explain.mesh-lines-parity: The built mesh differs from the manual line list. Rebuild the preview and check that no line was omitted or changed.
checks.explain.mesh-warning: The automatic mesher found geometry or spacing that may make the grid costly or inaccurate. Review the detail in this message and adjust the nearby geometry or mesh settings before running again.
checks.explain.metal-floating: This metal touches no other metal, no dielectric and no port, so it is an isolated conductor in the air that only coupling can reach. Move it onto the intended face or conductor; a deliberate parasitic element (a director, a reflector, a stacked patch) may stay as it is.
checks.explain.metal-overhang: This metal lies on a dielectric face but reaches past the dielectric's edge, so part of it hangs in the air where a printed conductor has no board. Shrink or move the metal, or enlarge the dielectric under it, unless the overhang is intended.
checks.explain.metal-thickness: A lossy metal sheet is modeled with a finite thickness, which must be positive. Enter the copper thickness in mm (0.035 for 1 oz copper), or leave it empty for the default 0.035 mm.
checks.explain.monitor-band: A current monitor outside the simulated band cannot give a reliable frequency result. Move its frequency into the band or expand the band to include it.
checks.explain.monitor-efficiency: The efficiency over the band is computed from the far-field box after the run, so it needs the far field and a usable number of frequencies. Turn the far field on and use a whole number of frequencies from 3 to 201; 21 is usually enough.
checks.explain.nf2ff-pec: The far-field box leaves out a face that lies on a PEC or PMC boundary (the wall mirrors it), so enabling that face has no effect. Turn the face off to match what is simulated; ground-plane and half-space models skip the face on the ground.
checks.explain.no-metal: There is no metal solid to carry the antenna current in this design. Add a conductor or assign a metal material to the intended conducting solid.
checks.explain.no-port: Without a port the design has no excitation or S-parameter measurement. Add a suitable lumped or waveguide port and connect it to the intended feed.
checks.explain.param-range: The parameter limits or default disagree, so edits and sweeps cannot use a consistent range. Put the minimum below the maximum and keep the default within those limits.
checks.explain.part-empty: This solid contains no shapes and contributes no geometry to the simulation. Add a shape or remove the unused solid.
checks.explain.part-hidden: Another solid with equal or higher priority fully covers this solid, so it has no effect on the simulation. Raise its priority if it should replace that material, move it, or remove it if unused.
checks.explain.part-name-duplicate: Two solids share a name, which makes selection and geometry references ambiguous. Give each solid a unique name.
checks.explain.polygon-area: The polygon points lie on a line, so the shape has no area. Move a vertex away from that line to give the outline a width.
checks.explain.polygon-points: A polygon needs at least three distinct vertices to enclose an area. Add or move points to form a closed outline.
checks.explain.polygon-self-intersect: The outline crosses itself, so its inside and outside are ambiguous. Reorder or move the vertices until only neighboring edges meet.
checks.explain.port-at-null: If this thin conductor is a resonant patch above a substrate and ground, a center feed can sit near a fundamental-mode voltage null and couple poorly. Move it off center along the resonant length if that matches your design; the fix button offers a starting offset to tune.
checks.explain.port-floating: This port endpoint touches no conductor, so the feed may not deliver current to the antenna. Move the endpoint onto the intended metal face and check both ends of the feed gap.
checks.explain.port-in-metal: Metal covers part of the port and can short its excitation. Place the endpoints on the facing conductor surfaces so the port spans only the gap between them.
checks.explain.port-length: The port has no length along its excitation direction, so it cannot drive or measure the intended field. Separate start and stop on that axis; an excited waveguide port needs at least a mesh cell between excitation and probe.
checks.explain.port-overlap: Overlapping ports drive or measure the same region and can interfere with each other. Move or resize the ports so their bounds do not touch or overlap.
checks.explain.port-r: The port impedance must be positive to define a physical load and meaningful S-parameters. Enter a positive resistance in ohms, commonly 50.
checks.explain.port-volume: A lumped port with width in both transverse directions fills a volume instead of the intended feed gap. Make it a line or sheet by matching start and stop on at least one transverse axis.
checks.explain.preview_unavailable: {reason} The mesh numbers and the server's checks shown are from the last successful preview, not from this draft; the list only has the checks made in the browser. Retry the preview (status bar) once the server responds.
checks.explain.radius: An invalid radius prevents the shape from being built. Use a positive radius; a cone may have one zero radius for a sharp tip.
checks.explain.resistor-length: The resistor has no extent along its current direction, so it cannot bridge a gap. Separate its endpoints on the selected direction axis.
checks.explain.resistor-r: A zero or negative resistance does not define the passive resistor expected here. Enter a positive resistance in ohms.
checks.explain.scale: Every primitive remains exact only under positive uniform scaling. Use the same positive factor on x, y and z; nonuniform or nonpositive factors are unsupported.
checks.explain.structure: The design contains an invalid or missing field, so further checks cannot safely inspect it. Correct the field named in the message and validate the design again.
checks.explain.tan-d: A negative loss tangent describes gain instead of a passive dielectric. Use zero for a lossless material or a positive loss tangent from its data sheet.
checks.explain.tan-d-band: openEMS models dielectric loss as a constant conductivity, so the loss tangent is exact only at the frequency given with it and scales as that frequency over f elsewhere. A datasheet value at 10 GHz used for a 2.45 GHz antenna makes its loss about four times too high. Give the frequency the design works at, for example f0, or leave the field empty for the band center.
checks.explain.tan-d-freq: The loss model needs a positive reference frequency to interpret the loss tangent. Enter the frequency in GHz at which the material's loss tangent was specified.
checks.explain.thin-metal: This thin conductor is simulated as a sheet so its thickness does not force tiny mesh cells and a very short timestep. No fix is needed for an intended sheet model; the thickness is kept for the losses and the exports. Metal at least 0.6 cells thick keeps its volume.
checks.explain.torus-radii: The tube radius reaches or crosses the torus axis, creating an unsupported shape. Make the minor radius smaller than the major radius and keep both positive.
checks.explain.polyhedron: A polyhedron is a closed solid. It needs at least 4 vertices and 4 faces, and every face lists at least 3 different vertex numbers that exist (0 up to the number of vertices minus 1).
checks.explain.polyhedron-flat: All the vertices lie in one plane on some axis, so the solid has no thickness. Move at least one vertex off that plane.
checks.explain.wg-aperture: The port cross-section does not match the dimensions used to calculate its mode field. Adjust the port bounds or a and b so the aperture and mode dimensions agree.
checks.explain.wg-cutoff: Below cutoff the selected mode does not propagate, so its S-parameters are not meaningful there. Raise the band above cutoff or enlarge the guide to lower cutoff.
checks.explain.wg-mode: The waveguide excitation needs a supported rectangular TE mode. Enter TEmn with single-digit indices, such as TE10, and do not use TE00.
checks.explain.wg-size: A waveguide needs a positive width and height to define its mode field. Set both a and b to positive dimensions in millimeters.
checks.explain.wire-points: The wire has no path unless it contains at least two distinct points. Add an endpoint or move a point away from the others.
checks.explain.wire-thin: The mesh is wider than the wire, so the simulated radius is controlled by the grid instead of the drawn radius. Increase the wire radius or refine the mesh across it and check convergence.
checks.explainFallback: Review the reported value and its settings. Edit the field below, then check the updated preview before running.

sim.mesh.thinMetal.note: Metal much thinner than a cell (e.g. 35 µm copper) becomes a zero-thickness sheet on its substrate side; its thickness would only shrink the timestep. The drawing keeps the thickness. "Mesh the thickness" keeps the volume only of metal at least 0.6 cells thick: thinner plates stay sheets, since cells across them would make the run many times longer and often never end.
sim.mon.currentsLegend: The 3D legend names the driven port. There are no per-port current maps.
sim.mon.currentsMulti: With several ports the solver runs once per driven port; only the first of these runs records currents, with the other ports terminated.
sim.mon.currentsNote: Surface-current maps are recorded on the metal sheets (zero-thickness bricks and polygons, up to 4 planes) at exactly these frequencies. After a run they are under Results › 2D/3D Results in the navigation tree.
sim.mon.currentsSingle: One excitation only: the maps are recorded in a single run, with one port driven.
sim.mon.effNeedsFarField: Needs the far field: turn it on above.
sim.mon.effNote: Radiation and total efficiency at {points} frequencies across the band; adds post-processing time, not solver time.
sim.mon.effRange: {min} to {max}, evenly spaced from f min to f max
sim.mon.ffFacesNote: The far-field box records the radiation through these faces. Ground-plane and half-space models skip the face on the ground (a PEC boundary). At least one face must stay on.

feed.coordinates: Enter the two endpoints explicitly. Nothing is added until you create it. Expressions and design parameters are supported.
feed.chipNote: Fill a physical passive parallel R/C or R/L load from the target impedance. It matches the target only at this frequency; its impedance changes elsewhere. This does not set a port power-wave reference. Frequency uses GHz (1 GHz = 1e9 Hz); generated L and C use H and F. Review the values and endpoints before creating the element.
feed.chipInvalid: Use a positive finite resistance and frequency, and a finite reactance. Values must yield finite positive components.
feed.seriesLimitation: Native series RLC is available, but the current circuit validation exceeded its 10% error criterion (21.7%). Verify circuit and mesh agreement before relying on its response.
feed.rlcNote: Leave unused R, L or C fields empty. Values use Ω, H and F (1e-9 H = 1 nH; 1e-12 F = 1 pF). These are physical passive time-domain loads; a complex reference impedance is a separate result convention.
feed.floquetNote: Floquet/Bloch ports and oblique periodic excitation are not supported by this solver workflow. PEC/PMC normal-incidence fixtures do not provide general Floquet modes.
feed.invalid: Check endpoints, direction and positive component values. Waveguide ports also require a valid TE mode, cross-section and propagation distance.
feed.referenceNote: Postprocessing only: Γ = (Zin − conj(Zref)) / (Zin + Zref). A conjugate match has Γ = 0. The physical source resistance remains real. To model a physical load, add a passive R/L/C element; a constant imaginary impedance is not a broadband time-domain load.
feed.muNote: Isotropic, loss-free and frequency-independent μr. Magnetic loss, tensors and dispersive ferrites are not represented.
checks.explain.mu-r: Relative permeability must be positive in the isotropic loss-free material model. Magnetic loss and dispersion are not represented.

checks.explain.port-reference: A complex power-wave reference is supported only on lumped ports and must contain exactly real and imag expressions. It is separate from the physical source resistance.
checks.explain.smallest-cell: The timestep follows the smallest cell, so the shape named here sets how long the run takes. Make that detail coarser, model thin metal as a sheet, or merge outlines that differ by a hair.
checks.explain.thin-metal-volume: Meshing thin metal as a volume needs cells a few micrometres wide. The timestep follows the smallest cell, so the run would need tens of times more timesteps and often never converge. Thin plates are therefore built as sheets even with thin metal set to volume; the sheet keeps the thickness for losses and exports.
checks.explain.run-too-long: The excitation pulse and the fields' decay after it would need more cells x timesteps than the run budget, usually because a tiny cell (thin metal kept as a volume, or two outlines a hair apart) forces a very small timestep. Remove the cause named in the message, or accept a long run by setting max timesteps yourself.
